title: How to learn good representations by prediction?
reading: The slide argues that images carry more redundant information than language, so the masking ratio used in masked prediction pretraining should be chosen per application. A line chart of MAE transfer accuracy versus masking ratio supports the point, with annotations contrasting the optimal masking level in language (BERT) against that in vision.

visuals.description: Line chart with triangle markers labelled 'MAE': x-axis 'masking ratio %' from 10 to 90, y-axis 'transfer accuracy' from 50 to ~75. Accuracy rises from ~55 at 10% to a peak ~73 near 70–75%, then falls to ~66 at 90%. Red annotations with arrows point to the 15% region and the 75% region.
visuals.assertion: Transfer accuracy for MAE peaks at a high masking ratio (~75%), unlike language where ~15% masking is optimal for BERT.

verbatim_spans: Information in images is more redundant than in languages
